problem: Spiking neural networks sacrifice energy-saving benefits as they scale to larger and deeper models.
approach: UniSparse combines weight pruning with spike sparsification by using batch-norm affine parameters as learnable neuron thresholds to reduce firing rates while maintaining accuracy.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art energy-accuracy trade-off; a sparsified ResNet-18 requires only 7.04M SOPs to reach 92.38% accuracy on CIFAR-10.

problem: Existing hallucination detectors for large language models rely on coarse attention summaries that miss fine-grained instabilities in grounding behavior.
approach: Uses frequency-domain analysis to extract high-frequency components from attention distributions during token generation, revealing hallucinated tokens exhibit high-frequency attention energy.
contribution: Lightweight detector achieves performance gains over verification, internal-representation, and attention-based methods on RAGTruth and HalluRAG benchmarks.

problem: Spiking neural networks for event-camera object detection suffer from noise sensitivity, dense representations disrupting spike pathways, and poor multi-scale feature perception.
approach: Proposes bio-vision-inspired architecture with noise-filtering STATNF-Neuron, Events-to-Spikes representation mimicking retinal properties, and bidirectional multi-scale spiking network.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance: 96.1% on NCAR, 63.5% mAP(50) on N-Caltech101, 69.1% mAP(50) on Gen1.

problem: Full-network linearization for Bayesian uncertainty quantification in deep neural networks is computationally expensive, so last-layer approximation is commonly used but its UQ capability cost is unclear.
approach: Uses random matrix theory and empirical evaluation to compare uncertainty quantification from full-network and last-layer linearization of Bayesian generalized linear models.
contribution: Last-layer linearization yields comparable UQ performance to full linearization while substantially improving computational efficiency.

problem: Test-time training with KV binding is interpreted as online meta-learning memorization, but empirical phenomena contradict this interpretation.
approach: Reformulates test-time training as learned linear attention operators, providing parallel formulations and systematic reduction of diverse TTT variants to standard linear attention.
contribution: Reframes TTT as learned linear attention rather than test-time memorization, enabling principled architectural simplifications and fully parallel formulations.

problem: Long-text understanding at million-token scale requires balancing reasoning fidelity with computational efficiency, as frontier LLMs suffer high token consumption and attention dilution.
approach: SCOUT shifts from passive processing to active information foraging by treating documents as explorable environments, using state-level gap diagnosis to guide adaptive exploration toward query-sufficient subsets.
contribution: Matches state-of-the-art performance while reducing token consumption by up to 8 times; remains stable as context length scales.

problem: Self-improvement training in large reasoning models suffers from data imbalance (simple samples dominate) and overthinking (redundant reasoning steps), leading to model collapse.
approach: HSIR introduces verify-then-exit sampling to collect accurate difficult solutions and Intrinsic Diversity scoring to filter undesired solutions; H-GRPO leverages diversity as an external reward.
contribution: Enhances reasoning performance by up to 10.9% and reduces inference overhead by up to 42.4%.

problem: Existing HDP-HMM and hidden semi-Markov models assume stationary state durations, limiting expressiveness for temporal data.
approach: Extends HDP-HMM with recurrent explicit duration modeling to allow observation-dependent durations; proposes Gibbs sampling for efficient inference.
contribution: RED-HDP-HMM consistently outperforms sticky HDP-HMM on segmentation tasks by incorporating state-duration flexibility.

problem: Transfer learning requires effective knowledge aggregation from diverse sources but lacks principled geometric foundations for model integration.
approach: Uses Riemannian geometry to align latent-space Ricci curvature across models, constructing GEAR architecture for unified transfer learning with comprehensive geometric representation.
contribution: Achieves at least 14.4% improvement on molecular task pairs under random splits and 8.3% under scaffold splits.

problem: Sequential Monte Carlo-based inference-time scaling relies on approximate reward models but lacks understanding of when and why they suffice.
approach: Identifies Bellman error as key quantity governing SMC effectiveness; shows bounded Bellman error enables exponential computational improvement despite approximate rewards.
contribution: For reasoning length T with O(1/T) Bellman error bound, reduces computational complexity from exponential to polynomial in T.

problem: Cybersecurity research is constrained by scarcity of labeled malware datasets; existing public datasets are obsolete and sandboxes fail to capture sample-specific behavioral dependencies.
approach: Threat2Traffic uses multi-agent framework to extract sample-specific dependencies from threat intelligence via evidence-graph deliberation and synthesizes tailored environments with dual-layer validation.
contribution: Achieves 83.1% reproduction success on 1,077 samples across eight malware families; releases source code and traffic dataset.

problem: Vision-Language Models show high decoding fidelity on visually compressed text but fail at reasoning on compressed modalities compared to native text.
approach: CoRe enforces lockstep consistency between text and visual reasoning policies via step-wise distribution matching; integrates into both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
contribution: Recovers up to 70% of performance gap between visual and textual modalities on mathematical reasoning, memory, and tabular retrieval tasks.

problem: Behavioral data is heterogeneous with diverse modalities and prediction targets, creating imbalanced learning dynamics that challenge foundation models for social behavior.
approach: OmniSapiens-7B 2.0 uses Heterogeneity-Aware Relative Policy Optimization to rebalance learning signals by approximating each sample's contribution and applying geometrically centered advantage modulation.
contribution: Best and most consistent performance across 10 behavioral tasks; gains of up to 12.02% on behavioral benchmarks and 9.37% on held-out tasks.

problem: Disaggregated LLM serving suffers from persistent load imbalance in memory-bound decode instances because output lengths are unknown at request arrival.
approach: MAPS performs device-assisted output length prediction overlaid with cloud prefilling; applies uncertainty-aware calibration and hierarchical scheduling to mitigate queue buildup.
contribution: Reduces average end-to-end latency by 42.6% and tail latency by up to 84.8% over state-of-the-art systems.

problem: Conditional time series generation lacks standardized benchmarking framework for systematic evaluation across diverse conditions and generation methods.
approach: ConTSG-Bench provides suite of large-scale, well-aligned datasets with diverse conditioning modalities and semantic levels; includes comprehensive metrics for fidelity and condition adherence.
contribution: Benchmarks reveal limitations and critical challenges in structural controllability and downstream task utility under complex conditions.

problem: Plasticity interventions are indispensable in modern deep RL agents but their impact on backdoor attack vulnerabilities remains unexplored.
approach: Empirically studies 14,664 cases combining representative plasticity interventions and attack scenarios; proposes SCC framework identifying mechanistic interplay and abnormal loss-landscape sharpness detection.
contribution: Finds SAM exacerbates backdoor threats while other interventions mitigate them; derives novel backdoor detection indicator via loss landscape analysis.

problem: Domain generalized object detection with vision foundation models uses fixed, style-agnostic parameters, overlooking how different visual styles induce distinct task discrepancies.
approach: SCoA introduces Spectral Style Modeling to preserve style cues and Mixture-of-Tokens Adaptation to dynamically route samples to optimal token combinations; SCQR injects style into detection heads.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art domain generalization performance by enabling style-specific adaptation trajectories.

problem: Validating functional equivalence of code translations and repairing inequivalent translations requires handling multiple programming languages with high engineering overhead.
approach: MatchFixAgent uses multi-agent LLM framework dividing validation into sub-tasks for thorough semantic analysis; performs language-agnostic equivalence checking and repair.
contribution: Produces verdicts for 99.2% of translation pairs; repairs 50.6% of inequivalent translations compared to prior work's 18.5%.

problem: Deep neural networks achieve high infrared-visible image fusion quality but existing methods are sophisticated and redundant, hindering deployment on mobile devices.
approach: MobileFusion uses re-parameterizable multi-branch convolution to enable cross-modal interaction during training while collapsing to single-path for inference; adds lightweight attention.
contribution: Delivers high-quality fusion on resource-constrained platforms with favorable trade-off between quality and computational efficiency.

problem: Softmax attention's nonlinear structure poses challenges for theoretical analysis of transformer learning dynamics.
approach: Uses measure-based framework showing softmax converges to linear operator under infinite prompts; establishes non-asymptotic concentration bounds for finite prompts.
contribution: Proves large-prompt softmax inherits linear attention's analytical structure; enables optimization analysis transfer to softmax for sufficiently long prompts.

problem: Computing expected information gain for sequential experiment design involves doubly intractable expectations, making optimization prohibitively expensive.
approach: Derives sufficient conditions allowing collapse to singly intractable expressions when posterior is exponential family; provides corresponding unbiased estimators.
contribution: Achieves superior convergence rates and substantial performance gains for sequential design compared to standard nested estimators.

problem: Continual reinforcement learning research focuses on only 3-10 sequential tasks due to CPU computational constraints; multi-agent continual RL remains unexplored.
approach: MEAL leverages JAX and GPU acceleration to enable training on 100-task sequences on single GPU in hours; combines continual and multi-agent settings.
contribution: Discovers failure modes in long task sequences not apparent at smaller scales; first benchmark for continual multi-agent RL.

problem: Multi-affine quadratic equality constrained problems are generally non-convex with convexity only when all variables except one are fixed, making optimization difficult.
approach: Proves alternating direction method of multipliers converges; shows linear convergence when non-convexity degree remains bounded.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees for ADMM on non-convex multi-affine problems with applications in robotics and neural network training.

problem: Multimodal large language models' capacity to interpret involuntary, spatio-temporally evolving pathologic motor behaviors like seizure semiology remains untested.
approach: Introduces Seizure-Semiology-Suite with 438 seizure videos and 35,000+ dense labels; proposes seven-task hierarchical benchmark and neuro-symbolic classification framework.
contribution: Achieves F1 score 0.96 on epileptic vs non-epileptic classification; establishes benchmark for safety-critical medical video understanding.

problem: Softmax attention's relationship to Bayesian inference lacks clear characterization beyond intuition that both normalize scores and log-probabilities.
approach: Shows softmax attention can implement exact Bayes posterior for finite latent symbols with exponential-family observations; characterizes representable posteriors as log-linear.
contribution: Establishes when Bayes-aligned attention admits globally shared quadratic metric via exponential-family duality; provides multi-head approximation with bounds.

problem: Model-based reinforcement learning via latent imagination is constrained by historical tethering where imagination initializes only from observed states, creating learning asymmetry.
approach: Mind Dreamer instantiates active causal intervention by drawing initial states from adversarial generator for non-continuous latent jumps; uses Relay Value Function for credit assignment.
contribution: Achieves 1.67x average speedup over DreamerV3 on DMC, reaching 8.8x on sparse-reward tasks.

problem: Optimization dynamics governing acquisition of deep semantic dependencies in large language models remain poorly understood.
approach: Proposes mechanistic framework modeling learning as competition between surface statistics and deep semantics; identifies gradient starvation suppressing error signals for sparse dependencies.
contribution: Shows Chain-of-Thought bypasses suppression regime; topology-aligned contrastive objective achieves 2x larger improvement than cross-entropy on variable binding.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA treat knowledge conflicts in continual learning as something to avoid rather than address directly.
approach: SABER reframes continual learning as structured conflict management; uses subspace alignment for shared representations, orthogonal decomposition for distinct knowledge, and energy-aware balancing.
contribution: Achieves performance on par with or surpassing state-of-the-art by directly managing representational conflict.

problem: Directly training generative models P(hypothesis|background) for scientific discovery is mathematically intractable due to combinatorial complexity O(N^k) in retrieving and composing inspirations.
approach: MOOSE-Star enables tractable training via decomposed subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical search enabling logarithmic retrieval, and bounded composition; releases TOMATO-Star dataset of 108,717 papers.
contribution: Reduces complexity from exponential to logarithmic O(log N); scales continuously while direct sampling hits complexity wall.

problem: Collecting sensitive data requires asymmetric privacy where certain values are more sensitive than others, but existing local-differential-privacy mechanisms require predefining sensitive regions.
approach: Introduces mechanism within Utility-Optimized Local Differential Privacy enabling censoring with plausible deniability; selectively withholds identifying details for sensitive content.
contribution: Avoids need to predefine sensitive region; provides theoretical guarantees including uniform consistency and pointwise weak convergence.

problem: Adapting large pretrained diffusion models to new tasks requires understanding the underlying frequency-energy mechanism governing denoising reconstruction.
approach: FeRA proposes frequency-driven fine-tuning with compact frequency-energy indicator, soft frequency router dynamically fusing expert adapters, and consistency regularization.
contribution: Provides simple, stable, compatible paradigm for effective diffusion model adaptation across backbones and resolutions.

problem: Integrating vision-language models into end-to-end autonomous driving suffers from distribution mismatch, underexploited reasoning, and high inference latency.
approach: AutoMoT unifies reasoning and action in single vision-language-action model using mixture-of-transformer with asynchronous multi-frequency inference; includes diffusion-based action refiner.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks with reduced inference latency.

problem: Training agents from experience data with reinforcement learning is difficult in environments lacking verifiable rewards or requiring inefficient long-horizon rollouts.
approach: Introduces early experience paradigm: agent-generated interaction data where resulting states provide supervision without reward signals; combines world modeling and self-reflection.
contribution: Consistently improves effectiveness and out-of-domain generalization; provides foundation for subsequent reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

problem: Large reasoning models generate long Chain-of-Thought sequences but emergent dynamics governing reasoning trajectories are poorly understood, leading to inconsistencies.
approach: Approximates reasoning dynamics as trajectory within finite state machine transitioning among six cognitive states; uses Q-Value guided steering to control reasoning as planning.
contribution: Achieves significant performance gains with surgical efficiency requiring 25x fewer interventions than baselines across AIME25, MATH-500, GSM8k, and GPQA Diamond.

problem: Existing long-context benchmarks focus on single-step retrieval and ignore context rot, where language agents reliability deteriorates under dynamically growing context.
approach: LOCA-bench leverages automated environment-state control to regulate agent context length while keeping task semantics fixed; enables extension to infinite contexts.
contribution: First benchmark for language agents under long-context conditions; shows advanced context-management techniques substantially improve success rates.

problem: Prior work on reward poisoning in reinforcement learning provides sufficient conditions for attacks but lacks understanding of when targeted poisoning is fundamentally infeasible.
approach: Establishes both necessary and sufficient conditions for reward-poisoning attackability in linear MDPs; characterizes vulnerable and intrinsically robust instances.
contribution: Draws clear boundary between vulnerable and robust RL instances; framework extends to deep RL by approximating as linear MDPs.

problem: Direct-mapping time series forecasting methods exhibit response lag around distribution shifts and regime changes, causing error accumulation and reduced reliability.
approach: L-Drive introduces latent-context to characterize high-level dynamics and uses gating to modulate increment representations; incorporates patch-shared relative positional basis functions.
contribution: Better overall trade-off between forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency; addresses change-aware forecasting.

problem: Existing periodic generative models sacrifice additivity in probabilistic modeling and become sensitive to schedule heuristics for wrap-around boundaries.
approach: PeriodicBFN embeds periodic scalars as two-dimensional unit-circle representations and performs Gaussian updates in Cartesian space; derives Rao-Blackwellized translation-invariant objective.
contribution: Restores strictly additive accuracy for periodic generative modeling; improves training stability for crystal structure and phase synthesis.

problem: LLM serving systems assume spatially uniform and temporally stable workloads but real-world heterogeneity in compute and memory demands is substantial and time-varying.
approach: OServe introduces workload-aware scheduling for heterogeneous model deployments and workload-adaptive switching enabling deployment migration in response to predicted changes.
contribution: Improves performance by up to 2x (average 1.5x) over state-of-the-art systems on real-world traces.

problem: Monocular normal estimation for transparent objects is critical for lab automation but fails due to complex light refraction, hindering embodied AI in scientific environments.
approach: TransNormal adapts diffusion priors via cross-attention to DINOv3 visual semantics; uses multi-task learning and wavelet regularization; introduces TransNormal-Synthetic physics-based dataset.
contribution: On ClearGrasp reduces mean error by 25.5%; on ClearPose achieves 17.7% error reduction.
